change_policy: After freeze, targets, labels, predictor set and split rules change only via a dated amendment in docs/protocol-v1.0.md §10, with reason; never after looking at test-fold results.
study: Detecting and explaining client-side Web performance degradation with Explainable ML

shopify_storefront.main_study: ≥ 30 stores × 2 pages, stratified random sample by reference TBT (W3)

controlled_testbed.role: one-factor-at-a-time fault injection with known cause for RQ3 (ground truth)

shopify_staging.role: case study before/after optimisation for RQ4

toolchain.browser: Google Chrome stable, headless=new; version recorded per row (chrome_user_agent)

measurement_profile.device: Lighthouse mobile emulation (412×823 viewport, mobile UA, touch)
measurement_profile.network: devtools throttling: request latency 562.5 ms, download 1474.56 Kbps, upload 675 Kbps (pinned in src/collector/lighthouse-collector.js)
measurement_profile.cache: cold — fresh Chrome profile per measurement; Lighthouse clears HTTP cache and storage
measurement_profile.order: all measurements of a batch shuffled with a fixed seed (default 42)
measurement_profile.timeouts: maxWaitForLoad 60 s; hard cap 150 s per measurement

primary.tbt_30s_ms: Σ max(0, d − 50 ms) of top-level main-thread tasks clipped to [FCP, min(navigationStart + 30 s, end of trace)], from the raw trace

outcomes.rationale_tbt_30s: Lighthouse TBT is undefined when TTI is never reached (heavy pages) — excluding them biases the sample toward fast sites.

validity_rules.V1_cross_host_redirect: main document or displayed URL leaves the requested site (subdomains allowed both ways) → invalid; Shopify /password, /challenge, /checkpoint → storefront_blocked (invalid)
validity_rules.V3_not_shopify: no asset from cdn.shopify.com or /cdn/shop on the main host → invalid
validity_rules.V4_host_contention: benchmark_index < 0.6 × median benchmark_index of the batch → invalid (measuring machine busy; timings inflated). Applied when the dataset is rebuilt (npm run reparse)
validity_rules.no_evasion: sites that block automated clients are excluded, never circumvented

never_in_X: all metadata (site, page_type, fault_*, severity_level, cause_group, run, order_index, benchmark_index, ...)
predictors.leakage_exclusions: per-target excludeFor in feature-definitions.js (trace_long_task_* excluded for tbt_30s_ms and lh_tbt_ms); empirical check |Spearman ρ| ≥ 0.95 in docs/leakage-checklist.md
predictors.mixed_group: request_count, transfer_bytes_total, mt_parse_html_ms: whole-page totals moved by every mechanism — kept in X, excluded from RQ3 group scores

cause_groups.main_thread_js: JavaScript execution blocking the main thread
cause_groups.dom_layout: large DOM, style recalculation and layout work
cause_groups.lcp_resource: heavy/slow resource of the LCP element
cause_groups.render_blocking: CSS/font that delays first render (testbed injects CSS only; font out of scope, protocol §4)
cause_groups.third_party: excessive third-party resources and their network/CPU cost

faults: src/testbed/fault-catalog.js — 6 faults (5 cause groups) × 3 severities + 1 shared baseline; one fault per condition; third-party-long-task is dose-matched to js-long-task (only the origin of the long tasks differs)

rq1_rq2_observational.primary: GroupKFold, k = 5, group = site (all pages and runs of a site in the same fold); fold = int(sha1('fold:' + site)[:8], 16) mod 5
rq1_rq2_observational.lockbox: sites with int(sha1('lockbox:' + site)[:8], 16) mod 5 == 0 (~20%) are held out until the final evaluation

rq3_testbed.primary: GroupKFold over run index (5 folds): train on 4 repetitions of every condition, explain the held-out repetition
